name: Helix Tower
blurb: A diagrid super-structure that cut steel tonnage by 22 percent against a conventional frame.
overview: Helix Tower is a 44 storey commercial high rise on the Elbe waterfront. The brief asked for column free floor plates and a slender profile, so we developed a perimeter diagrid that carries both gravity and lateral load without an internal core wall. Every node was resolved parametrically and checked under full non linear seismic and wind analysis.

name: North Crossing
blurb: A twin pylon bridge carrying road and light rail across a fjord that sees severe cross winds.
overview: North Crossing carries road and light rail across the Aarhus fjord on a twin pylon cable stayed deck. The site sees severe cross winds and an aggressive marine environment, so the deck section was wind tunnel tested and the stay anchorages detailed for inspection and replacement without closing the crossing.

name: Atlas Process Plant
blurb: A heat recovery redesign of a continuous process line, recommissioned with no downtime.
overview: Atlas asked us to cut the energy load of an ageing continuous process line without stopping production. We metered the plant for a full season, built a model against the measured baseline, and staged the heat recovery installation across four scheduled maintenance windows.

name: Meridian Transit Hub
blurb: A long span steel canopy and below grade concourse built over live tracks.
overview: Meridian is an interchange that had to be built over and around live tracks. The signature is a 96 metre clear span canopy that shelters the platforms without a column between them. Erection ran in 41 possessions of four hours each, with the stability case checked at every stage.

name: Kade Viaduct
blurb: An elevated freight route through a working port, built without closing a berth.
overview: The viaduct carries freight traffic over a congested quayside. Foundations thread between existing services and a live rail spur, so each pile position was proved with radar before it was set out. The deck is precast to keep occupation of the quay to a minimum.

name: Haven Terminal
blurb: A process terminal erected alongside a plant that stayed in production throughout.
overview: Haven Terminal adds storage and processing capacity to an operating site. Everything above the foundations was assembled in modules off site and lifted in during three planned shutdowns, which kept the crane time on the live plant to nine days in total.

name: Westgate Foundations
blurb: A single raft pour under a mixed use block, on ground that varies across the site.
overview: Ground conditions across the Westgate site change from dense sand to soft clay within thirty metres, which ruled out a uniform pad solution. We designed a stiffened raft with local ground improvement and poured it in one continuous operation to avoid a construction joint under the core.

name: Delta Refinery Upgrade
blurb: A capacity upgrade tied into live systems inside a nine day shutdown window.
overview: The upgrade required 42 tie ins to systems that could only be opened during the annual shutdown. Every cut was rehearsed on the model and dry run on site, and the work package was sequenced so that no two tie ins competed for the same crane.

name: Brede Distribution Centre
blurb: A portal framed distribution centre delivered from ground investigation to handover in sixteen months.
overview: A large shed is a simple structure with an unforgiving programme. Connections were detailed to the fabricator's shop standards, steel arrived in erection sequence, and the slab was poured in bays that followed the frame rather than the other way round.

name: Zuidas Tower Retrofit
blurb: Six storeys added to a 1970s frame, with the building occupied throughout.
overview: The existing frame had capacity nobody had ever calculated, so we started with a full assessment and a load test rather than an assumption. Strengthening was targeted at eleven columns and two transfer beams, which was enough to carry the new storeys without touching the tenanted floors.

name: Scheldt Lock Gates
blurb: Replacement lock gates fabricated off site and floated into position in one tide.
overview: The gates were too large to assemble in place, so they were built on a quay, load tested there, and floated to the lock on a single tide. The mechanical drives were commissioned dry before the chamber was flooded.

name: Noord Campus
blurb: Four teaching buildings on a shared low temperature heat network.
overview: The campus runs on a low temperature network fed by ground source, which only works if the buildings are commissioned as a system rather than one at a time. Instrumentation was specified at design stage so that performance could be proved against the model before handover.
